scientific_update.semantic: Every genuinely fresh R19 world that produced a complete candidate and complete full-domain witness matched exactly. Six fresh worlds span both workload suites and n=24,32,40,56. No semantic counterexample was observed.
scientific_update.resource: R19 is not a ten-of-ten pass. Four frozen worlds produced no candidate result before the frozen five-minute job envelope. Their outcomes remain OPEN_EXECUTION_RESOURCE_LIMIT and cannot be promoted to semantic PASS or FAIL.
scientific_update.scaling: The completed ladder already shows strong instance dependence: candidate time ranges from ~0.023 s to ~24.7 s and maximum DAG nodes from 519 to 58,211. The four timeouts show that the current exact Shannon/hash-cons representation still has a severe resource-growth wall on some instances.
scientific_update.resource_contract_bug: The candidate's nominal internal 120-second deadline is cooperative and can be overrun by a single long pure-Python DAG operation before the next budget check. Therefore the external five-minute job timeout is the authoritative execution witness for the four missing worlds. This is an observability/resource-enforcement defect, not semantic evidence.
